reasoning_traces.think:
The multi-scale graph wavenet integrates spatial and temporal dimensions using a learned adjacency matrix and dilated convolutions. The adjacency matrix A = Softmax(E·E^T) dynamically encodes inter-station influences from learned embeddings E, allowing the model to adapt to local wind behavior rather than relying on fixed geographic distances. Temporal modeling uses dilated convolutions with exponentially increasing dilation to capture long-range dependencies in wind speed history. This dual approach enables accurate forecasting across 6/12/18/24-hour horizons. Failures occur when data is insufficient for learning adjacency or when temporal patterns exceed the dilation range. The model’s strength lies in its ability to generalize from multivariate time series of wind speeds at multiple stations, making it suitable for GSE's stadium weather network.
